steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease a 2 quart baking dish.
Spoon about one heaping quarter cup of pie filling evenly down the center of each tortilla. Sprinkle with cinnamon; roll up, tucking in edges; and place seam side down in prepared dish.

In a medium saucepan over medium heat, combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar and water. Bring to a boil, stirring constantly; reduce heat and simmer 3 minutes. Pour sauce over enchiladas and let stand 30 minutes.
Bake in preheated oven 20 minutes, or until golden.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Enchiladas
raw_recipe.description: Flour tortillas filled with apple pie filling and smothered in a simple syrup are baked until sweet and golden.
raw_recipe.name: Apple Enchiladas

review.reviewBody: I used whole wheat tortillas, and the end result was nice and chewy (not tough, as other reviewers have said). The sweetness of the apples and sauce was well-balanced by the nutty flavor of the wheat torillas. Also, I made my own apple pie filling, using about 4 cups of thinly sliced apples, about 2/3c. white sugar, 2Tbsp. flour, a little water, and cinnamon and nutmeg to taste. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer until apples soften (about 5 minutes)

Being a southern boy, I'm not going to tell you that this is BETTER than good ol' flaky crust apple pie, but it is good. As written, it's real good. However, if you want "OMG!, I can't stop sneaking in for another bite", try this: smear 1/6 of a brick of plain, softened cream cheese on the tortilla before the apple. Chop up the pie filling a little, and mix the cinnamon right in. Use "No Sugar Added" apple pie filling. An 8X12 dish spread it out better. Reduce water to about 1/3 or 1/4c. Bake for at least 40 minutes to get a crispy top. Topping it off with anything less than Blue Bell Homemade Vanilla Ice cream while it's still scalding hot is simply a compromise. To reiterate: as written if very good, but with these changes, you might want a smoke.

I used a no sugar added apple pie filling in one batch. I forgot to add the cinnamon to the filling, so I added pumpkin pie spice to the sauce instead.
I did a second batch using mixed berry pie filling. This kind has less fruit and more "filling" in the can, so I supplemented by adding a large handful of fresh blueberries before rolling up. For the sauce, I omitted the cinnamon and added vanilla instead.
Definitely needed at least 40 minutes of cooking time (and even that didn't leave them crispy, but that might be my oven's fault).
I didn't get to try it myself, but I have heard that they were a big hit at the pot luck!!

I made this for a Christmas book club dinner and chose it because it was dairy free. It was delicious & a huge hit with everyone! Lots of changes were made. I sliced up an apple & cooked with 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, 1/4 cup apple juice & 2 Tbsp. Brown sugar, until tender & mixed in the canned Apple filling. For the glaze, 1/2 cup Apple juice. 1/3 cup coconut oil, 1Tbsp. Cornstarch & 1 Tbsp. Brown sugar, & 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon until thicken. This makes enough to cover all the enchiladas, no tough enchiladas here. This is very easy & delicious!!

I was very pleasantly surprised at how good this came out! I did make a few changes though. Since I have about 50lbs of apples sitting on my table, I used fresh apples and mixed them with cinnamon and a bit of Mace (Allspice would also work). I then added about 1/2 cup of diced cold Brie to the apple mixture and 1 cup of dried cranberries soaked in water. Since I used rice tortillas, they were not as flexible as wheat so I made mine more like a lazagna-style instead of wrapping. Also, for the sauce, I didnt have enough brown sugar so I used a small amount of molasses. If you do this, it makes it REALLY rich so go light and save the extra to add when you serve it. I also added a mixture of cheddar and dublinger cheese on the top layer with the sauce. Bake covered as normal, and enjoy! 
I have extra sauce that I am going to try mixing with a Mexican mole sauce to see if I can make this more of a meal instead of a dessert. Either way, It came out REALLY good!

If you need a quick dessert and have the ingredients on hand this works. It is very sweet. I used wheat tortillas and a can of fried apple slices in cinnamon. I drained the apples and cut them into bite size pieces. Make sure you cover the ENTIRE enchilada with the sauce if you want a softer enchilada. The ends of the roll can get tough and chewy. Too avoid this you can use brush to sauce or just cover with foil the first 10 minutes of baking. When I made the sauce I used half of the apple juice from the can with half the amount of water to give more flavor. I did not add the cinnamon because it came in the apple filling. Served warm with vanilla ice cream. Not nearly as good cold or the next day.

This dessert is AMAZING! I am studying abroad right now and didn't have access to apple pie filling, so I chopped up 5 apples and simmered them with water, cinnamon and some sugar. I followed the rest of the recipe as listed. They were so rich that we could only have half each-with ice cream of course! People throughout the hall were coming in and wondering what smelled so delicious. Huge hit- I'm now a floor favorite :)

This turned out heavenly. I'm not sure why others said their sauce turned out watery with 1/2 cup of water. I think those people must have skipped the step where you let your sauce sit for 30 minutes on the enchiladas. Next time I'm going to double the sauce (1 cup sugar, 1 cup b. sugar, 1 cup water) because we loved it and there wasn't enough to go around! Also, we baked it for 35 minutes to get the outside good and golden brown. Turned out great!

Nice recipe- but here's what I did...I stuffed and rolled the tortillas as directed, and made the sauce as directed. Then I spooned a small amount onto each roll, just enough to wet the tops. While baking for ten minutes to get a crispy caramelized roll I added a small amount of condensed milk to the remaining sauce and simmered while the rolls were baking. After baking for ten minutes I covered with the remaining sauce. I let this set long enough to cool to a creamy consistency and topped with crushed walnuts.

I'm a novice baker and found this recipe easy to follow with excellent results. I had to make it within the prescribed hour and whisk it out the door for book club. It was a crowd pleaser and I will certainly make it again. To avoid the tough ends I brushed the sauce during the baking process several times. I added vanilla extract and nutmeg for extra flavor.

All I can say is WOW!! I did change a few things only because I had something like this at Carlos Okellys an we loved it. I used pie filling an added brown sugar an cinnamon to the mixture and I also mixed cinnamon with 8oz cream cheese an piped it down the center of the filling Then I DEEP FRIED it didnt want to wait all that time to bake im impatiant an then I served them with caramel ice cream topping an cinn an sugar. again WOW!!! Thank you
Too runny need more sugar. It was tough texture.

Such a beautiful dish. Do whatever you will with the seasonings that go into it, as long as they get hydrated and cooked. I have to more than double the recipe for my family, but i dont think thats really a bad thing. Having a side of cream cheese or whipped cream is always a plus for anyone that wants it. Ice cream is always a huge plus for the right crowd. I even had somebody ask for a slice of cheddar. Do not be fooled by the simplicity of this dish! There may be tears shed.
The enchiladas were very tasty, but they were soggy on the bottom. Maybe too much liquid?
Family all love this, so easy to make, my husband can make it. Good with vanilla ice cream
Easy to make. The family loved it.
It was good, but not outstanding. I wouldn't make it again.

Didn’t like this one. I made it and the only thing I changed was using all brown sugar in the sauce. The sauce did not blend well and the butter separated. It just seemed like was too much butter. The tortillas I used (mission brand) must have had too much salt or something because there was an underlying flavor that just didn’t fit. I’ll stick tie eating apple pie.
